caption:
This morning: OpenAI says Codex and ChatGPT now help design CAD models, PCBs and simulations, with hardware-team usage up 23x. Usage is not proof of results.

I went back in. On OpenAI's BenchCAD 2.0, Astra scores 0.594. Output costs $50 per million tokens, versus $10 for GPT-6.1 Sol. In an outside CAD Arena test, Astra averaged 0.671 against 0.662 for Claude Fable 5.1.

My take: a benchmark score says little about your own drawings. Test the model on your real parts, and count the review rounds.

Comment REVIT and I will send you the details by DM.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: The morning post said OpenAI now uses Codex for CAD, PCB and simulation, with model usage up 23x. I went back in to check the numbers around it.
First, on OpenAI's newer BenchCAD 2.0, GPT-6 Astra at top reasoning scores 0.594. The unreleased internal model scores 0.875.
Second, Astra's output costs $50 per million tokens. GPT-6.1 Sol costs $10, so heavy CAD iteration gets expensive fast.
Third, in an outside CAD Arena test across five platforms, Astra averaged 0.671. Claude Fable 5.1 was close at 0.662.
My take: a benchmark score says little about your own drawings. Test the model on your real parts, and count the review rounds.
